ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the positive terminal of the power supply U is at the upper left, first passing through the horizontally connected R1 to reach the upper node on the right; this upper node is connected downward through R2 to the bottom return node, and at the same time there is also a capacitor C on the right connected between the same upper node and the same bottom return node. Therefore, R2 and C are in parallel, and R1 is in series with this parallel branch. Reasoning: Given U = 100 V, R1 = 600 Ω, R2 = 400 Ω. In the DC steady state, the current in the capacitor branch is 0 and it can be regarded as an open circuit, but the voltage across the capacitor equals the voltage across R2, which is in parallel with it. Thus the circuit is equivalent to R1 and R2 in series voltage division, and the capacitor voltage is U_C = U × R2/(R1 + R2) = 100 × 400/(600 + 400) = 40 V.
